ART 3614.d: Students in this course are introduced to specialized materials and processes in ceramics. Emphasis is on developing focused skills in a specific topic related to both historical and contemporary ceramic art. The instrumental case for learning to make multiples rests on the human act of fabrication and sited decision-making, which persists even as the market for images and objects transforms and as AI handles ever more of the written and research scaffolding around the studio work itself.
ART 3616.d: Students in this course explore the nature of multiples and repetition in art while also focusing on research methods to connect concept generation, material choices, and production to the site of art projects. Research topics include the responsibility of artists to understand the history, ecological concerns, and prior and current uses of a material and/or site. The applied tasks — producing animations, designing characters, blocking timing — are broadly exposed, with no embodiment, licensure, or foundational cap to hold the rating down. What survives is narrower: the conceptual and storytelling judgment to direct and verify AI-generated motion, a real but partial residual given the jagged frontier where users outside the model's competence misjudge output. The instrumental case erodes meaningfully, hedged by the persistent need for a human who can shape and check the sequence.

A decade out, generative systems will fluently produce animated sequences, character designs, and storyboards to a professional standard, and the applied work this course's knowledge serves — making 2D animations — will be performed competently by AI with limited human input in the central case. With no embodiment, no licensure, and no strong foundational role protecting it, little caps the exposure. The rating is High, hedged by the wide uncertainty of ten-year forecasting and by the possibility that human direction of tone, pacing, and narrative retains a verification premium the tools do not supply. ART 3625.d: In this course, students learn to animate by examining movement and timing, exploring different techniques, and studying historical and contemporary animation practices. With an emphasis on storytelling, students produce a series of 2D animations, which begin with storyboard development and character designs. This course emphasizes research and conceptual thinking while incorporating art and design methods. This is an Integrated Media course.

The most plausible change is that technical execution moves almost entirely to AI while human curatorial and conceptual judgment about an artwork's impact remains — a real but bounded competence that does not, in the central case, preserve the broad instrumental need to learn the production tasks by hand.
ART 3632.d: Students in this course expand their knowledge using advanced technology to create emerging art. Students develop skills to create immersive art, including 2D and 3D game design, creative coding, sound recording, performance, and multimedia installation. Additionally, participants engage in critical thinking to understand the impact of emerging artworks on contemporary art. This course incorporates art and technology, preparing students to develop impactful and transformative immersive projects.

Absent any licensure or accreditation lock, embodiment and interpersonal presence hold the instrumental case at Low across this horizon. The plausible shift is that project administration and outreach text migrate to AI while the field-based, contextual engagement does not. The surrounding funding and art-world economics may change, but that is outside this rating; the need to learn to work dialogically with communities persists.

Over a decade, AI will absorb much of the administrative and communicative scaffolding around participatory art, and one can imagine tools that help design and analyze community engagement. But the specific competence this course builds — situated, ethically-weighty, real-time practice with communities in public spheres — is not a task AI executes on the artist's behalf, and embodiment plus interpersonal presence keep it among the lowest-exposure activities even at 2036. The genuine uncertainty is how much project logistics automate around a still-human relational core, not whether that core remains necessary. The rating holds Low; if anything, heavier AI mediation of communication raises the premium on artists who can judge when an automated engagement rings false. The instrumental case rests on the human capacity to convene and act contextually, which endures.
ART 3637.d: Students in this course are introduced to the field of socially engaged art through an emphasis on conversations, communities, situations, participation, places, aesthetics, and activism. Course content demonstrates the increasing use of relational and dialogical aesthetics informing conceptual and formal structures in contemporary art and design. Socially Engaged Art adopts a field- based model for its curriculum that is designed to provide students with opportunities to work contextually in a variety of public spheres. This is an Integrated Media course.

ART 3639.d: Students in this course explore performance as a major paradigm informing the methods and languages of contemporary practices in art and design. Emphasis is placed on border crossings, porous disciplines, and contingent identities as a central component in performance-based studio practice. Lectures and discussions engage the historically shifting nature of embodiment in contemporary art and design. This is an Integrated Media course.

AI competently drafts research prose and can generate images, so the paper and reference-image tasks carry exposure, since writing ranks high in task-exposure research, but the integrative core, producing a personal body of studio work animated by the student's own investigation and defending it live, is embodied and self-directed. There is no licensure or accreditation lock; embodiment and the capstone's synthesizing role bind. At 24 months the instrumental need to conduct and externalize a personal studio investigation is not eroded.

By 2031, AI will fluently draft research papers, structure arguments, and produce reference imagery, automating much of the written and preparatory scaffolding around the project. But the graded competence, developing a personal studio investigation, realizing it in one's own artwork, and presenting it live to an audience, remains embodied and interpersonal, and judging whether the visual work genuinely answers the student's question is a human assessment. Productivity studies show large AI writing gains, which sharpens the tension around the research-paper artifact, yet the studio making and live presentation are not tasks a model performs for the student. Absent institutional mandate, embodiment and the capstone function hold the instrumental case at Low across a catalog cycle. AI offloads the writing scaffold while leaving the studio investigation and its defense intact.

A decade out, AI will draft sophisticated research writing and generate imagery on demand, and the plausible shift is toward the paper and preparatory materials automating around a still-embodied studio-and-presentation core. But the specific thing this capstone builds, framing a personal artistic question, investigating it through one's own making, and externalizing it publicly, is not a task AI executes for the student. The rating holds Low in the central case through 2036, anchored by embodiment and the integrative senior-experience function rather than any mandate. The honest uncertainty concerns how the research and writing components are produced and assessed under ubiquitous AI, not whether an art student still needs to conduct and present their own studio investigation. The making and the live defense remain the student's to perform.
ART 4710.d: Students in this course find a problem or question to investigate within their studio art practice. Using academic methods and resources to support research, students externalize the integration of these concepts through their visual art, a research paper, and a public presentation. This is a Senior Experience course.

r: The assistantship puts advanced students to work supporting a studio: demonstrating and critiquing technique, running laboratories, maintaining tools and equipment, mixing chemicals where appropriate, stocking supplies, and helping peers with technical and creative questions in real time. The applied competence is embodied and interpersonal, hands-on equipment management and in-person instructional support in a physical studio, which task-exposure research places firmly among the least automatable, manual and interpersonal categories. AI can answer technical questions in the abstract, but it cannot mix chemicals, maintain a kiln or press, or demonstrate a physical technique at a student's side. There is no licensure lock; embodiment is decisive. At 24 months the instrumental need to develop hands-on studio-management and peer-instruction competence is untouched; no model performs the physical, in-room work the role consists of.

By 2031, AI tutoring tools will more capably field students' conceptual and technical questions, offloading some of the informational side of the assistant's role. But the embodied duties, maintaining equipment, preparing materials and chemicals safely, and demonstrating physical technique in the studio, are not tasks a model executes, and their failure modes, a mishandled chemical or a damaged press, carry real physical consequence, keeping a knowledgeable human present. Task-exposure frameworks consistently rank manual, in-person work low, and no diffusion trend puts a robot in the studio darkroom or ceramics lab on this horizon. Absent any mandate, embodiment holds the instrumental case at Low across a catalog cycle. AI augments the question-answering while leaving the physical studio-management and hands-on demonstration core, the point of the assistantship, intact.

A decade out, AI will handle much of the informational and even some diagnostic support a studio assistant provides, and the role could lean further toward the embodied tasks. But maintaining equipment, preparing materials, and demonstrating physical technique at a learner's side remain non-substitutable in the central case through 2036, because they are manual and in-person by nature. The rating holds Low, anchored by embodiment rather than any institutional lock. The genuine uncertainty concerns how much of the advisory component automates around a still-physical studio-support core, not whether the assistantship's hands-on competence is still needed. If anything, studios adopting more tooling raise the value of assistants who can maintain and demonstrate it; the embodied work does not migrate to a model.
ART 4801.d: This studio course allows the advanced student to put into use the studio skills learned in previous courses to assist faculty and other students through demonstrating and critiquing. Students will learn to run laboratories, maintain tools and equipment, mix chemicals (if appropriate), and handle and stock supplies in an appropriate manner. The applied competence is the embodied, self-directed act of making art and cultivating a personal artistic voice. Image-generation models produce pictures capably, creating conceptual tension, but they do not perform the psychomotor making or the individuated aesthetic judgment the student must develop; task-exposure research places the physical creative act outside the strongly-exposed programming and writing categories. There is no licensure or accreditation lock; embodiment does the protective work, exactly as in intermediate studio courses. At 24 months the instrumental need to produce a personal, finished body of studio work is not eroded, since generative tools reshape the art economy, not the independent studio act itself.

By 2031, generative image tools will be ubiquitous and will reshape commercial creative markets, an economic and enrollment matter outside this rating. Whether a directed-studies student still needs embodied, self-directed studio practice to develop an individual style and coherent body of work is unchanged: the material handling and personal aesthetic judgment are the competence, and they resist substitution. Some adjacent tasks, such as generating reference or compositional studies, plausibly migrate to AI, but the making does not. Absent any institutional mandate, embodiment alone holds the instrumental case at Low across this horizon, mirroring the intermediate-painting pattern. The discipline's market exposure is high and rising; the course's task-necessity, grounded in the human act of making and the cultivation of voice, is not. AI is a tool here, not a substitute for producing the work.

Over ten years, AI image generation will pervade visual culture and much commercial image production, and the wide-uncertainty caveat genuinely applies to the visual-arts labor market. But Directed Studies in Studio Art builds an embodied human competence, sustained independent making and an individuated artistic voice, that is not a task AI performs on the student's behalf. Base automatability ticks up modestly as generative tools encroach on adjacent applied work, yet embodiment keeps the rating Low even at 2036. The honest framing is the studio pattern: the instrumental case for producing one's own finished body of work rests on the human act of making, which endures even as the market for images transforms. No credible central-case path removes the need for the student to actually create the work themselves.
ART 4841.d: Students in the course produce advanced, independent studio work with emphasis on the production of finished work. The students integrate techniques, materials, and skills learned in previous courses to develop an individual style and create a coherent body of work.

r: This directed study has advanced students produce finished communication-design work, building an individual voice and a coherent body of work in preparation for the senior exhibition. Unlike embodied studio painting, communication design is a predominantly digital practice: layout, typography, image composition, and visual-messaging deliverables executed on the computer. Generative and design-assistant models are increasingly capable at producing such artifacts, and observed-usage data show creative and computer-based tasks are a prominent, growing share of AI use, so the applied production tasks carry real and rising exposure with limited embodiment protection. What resists automation on this horizon is the higher-order direction, conceiving a distinctive voice and curating a cohesive portfolio, and GDPval evidence shows models approaching but still below expert parity on real deliverables. At 24 months the instrumental need to develop personal design judgment through finished work is only modestly eroded; rating Low.

By 2031, generative design tools will fluently produce layouts, iterate visual concepts, and draft finished communication-design deliverables, materially automating the execution this directed study's work is applied to. With no embodiment, licensure, or accreditation lock to protect it, the instrumental case erodes more than for embodied studio courses: the rationale shifts from producing the artifacts oneself toward directing, curating, and critically judging AI-generated design and assembling a portfolio that reads as a distinctive voice. That art-directional competence keeps the course from becoming fully substitutable, but task-exposure research classifies digital creative production as genuinely exposed, pushing the rating to Medium. The honest read: much of the making automates, while the judgment of what is worth making, and whether a coherent voice has emerged, remains the student's, though even that is increasingly AI-assisted rather than AI-proof on this horizon.

A decade out, the central case has AI competently generating most communication-design production, with the designer's role centered on direction, curation, and client-facing judgment. The execution rationale for a portfolio directed study is substantially eroded, and with no institutional lock or embodiment to cap it, the rating holds Medium rather than staying Low. What sustains a residual instrumental need is the human capacity to set creative direction, evaluate whether AI-generated work achieves a distinctive and coherent voice, and take accountability for the result, competencies that grow more valuable as generation commoditizes, echoing the jagged-frontier caution about uncritical trust in AI output. The genuine uncertainty is how much high-level design direction itself automates by 2036; the rating stays Medium, not High, because that directional judgment remains meaningfully human in the central case.
ART 4842.d: This course provides advanced, independent studio work in communication design with emphasis on the production of finished work in preparation for the senior exhibition. The student will integrate techniques and skills learned in previous courses to develop an individual voice and create a coherent body of work.
